description: An open-source long-horizon SuperAgent harness that researches, codes, and creates. With the help of sandboxes, memories, tools, skill, subagents and message gateway, it handles different levels of tasks that could take minutes to hours.

summary.one_liner: DeerFlow is an open-source "super agent harness" from ByteDance that coordinates sub-agents, memory, sandboxes, and extensible skills to carry out research, coding, and content creation tasks that can run for minutes to hours.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes DeerFlow 2.0 as a ground-up rewrite (sharing no code with v1, whose Deep Research framework lives on the 1.x branch) that orchestrates sub-agents, memory, and sandboxes, extended through skills and tools. It supports multiple LLM providers via LangChain-style model configs in config.yaml, including OpenAI-compatible gateways, vLLM, Responses API, and CLI-backed providers such as Codex CLI and Claude Code OAuth. It integrates web search and fetch backends (for example Tavily, Jina, DuckDuckGo, SearXNG, InfoQuest, Brave) and an optional MCP server, IM channels, and ACP agent entries. Setup is driven by a `make setup` wizard that writes config.yaml and .env, with Docker (recommended) and local development paths, plus tracing options (LangSmith, Langfuse, Monocle). The README also covers projects, scheduled tasks, a terminal TUI, a managed model catalog in the web UI, and a Python embedded client.
use_cases: Long-running automated deep research on a topic
Autonomous coding and code-editing tasks inside a sandbox
Running multi-agent workflows with sub-agents and shared memory
Self-hosting an AI agent with configurable LLM providers
Building custom skills and MCP-connected tools for an agent
Generating reports, podcasts, or other created artifacts from research
notable: Sub-agent orchestration with memory and isolated sandboxes for long-horizon tasks
Interactive setup wizard (make setup) that generates config.yaml and .env
Broad model support, including Responses API, vLLM, Codex CLI, and Claude Code OAuth
Many pluggable web search and fetch backends with documented failure handling
Official website with demos and a sister desktop tool, LLM Space
caveats: The README warns that improper deployment can introduce security risks, and that gateway admin access is equivalent to code execution
Recommended hardware is substantial (16 GB RAM or more for a server), and Linux with Docker is the recommended persistent deployment; macOS and Windows are treated as dev or evaluation environments
Docker Compose v2.24+ is required; some search and model features need API keys or paid provider accounts
keywords: chat with ai that browses the web
